items.title: Decide how a migrated keys::Action leaves the enum without bypassing the Typing guard (E-024 is blocked on this)
items.evidence: Decided by the developer 2026-10-22: actions name their operation. A keys::Action counts as migrated when its binding dispatches a registered operation, checked mechanically (the action names its operation id; the parity test verifies the id against the registry and that the UI path dispatches it). The Typing guard stays, because the action stays in keys::Action. The parity test's definition of 'migrated' changes accordingly, and the allowlist keeps shrinking: lower UNMIGRATED_MAX by one per migrated action. the_allowlist_of_unmigrated_actions_only_shrinks asserts UNMIGRATED.len() == Action::ALL.len() and that every variant is listed by name (operations_have_two_front_ends.rs ~400-421). Action is generated by enumerated! (keys.rs ~504-833), so a migrated action must be removed from the enum for the ratchet to shrink. Options: (a) bind the key straight from KeyboardInput in editor.rs, which must re-create the keys::Context Typing guard; (b) let keymap bindings name an operation so the enum keeps only human-only verbs. Option (b) is the design the parity rule implies. Needs a developer decision before E-024 can ship.

items.title: Undoing an agent's turn takes one Cmd+Z per operation: a turn is not one undo step

must_fix.evidence: The brief: "An agent's multi-step action is grouped into one undo step, so a single undo reverts the whole agent step." Measured before: three `placement_add` operations then one Cmd+Z left TWO placements on the map (the third undone only), because each operation was its own `Undo::Logged`. After: one Cmd+Z leaves none, and a person's edit made before the turn is still standing and still undoable in its own right.

items.evidence:
Behaviour note (mixar@39b9d27).

Trigger: an agent presents a result — `emerge/present`, the same call that puts the Keep/Undo all question on screen.

Person sees: the confirmation card as before. What changes is the keyboard: ONE Cmd+Z now takes back everything the presented turn did, where it used to take back one operation and leave the rest. The INSPECTOR's UNDO row reads "3 changes" instead of naming one placement.

Agent gets: `grouped` in `emerge/present`'s answer — how many of the turn's entries became one (0 when it presented one operation, or ids the stack no longer holds). So it can say "one undo takes this back" only when that is true.

State: the turn's leaves on the editor's undo stack are folded into one `Undo::Group`, in the order the operation log can answer (newest first). Nothing is written to the map or the log; undo and redo both walk the group, and the group is closed under inversion like every other entry.

Refuses: nothing new. A presentation naming an id that is not in the log was already refused, and still is. A presentation naming no operations groups nothing, so a turn that changed nothing cannot swallow the person's next edit.

Differs: Mixar snapshots the whole document to a file before each turn and restores it; bevy_emerge has no whole-document snapshot and does not gain one. It groups the turn's own logged leaves instead, which is smaller, needs no disk budget, and keeps one source of truth (the oplog) rather than two. Mixar's position is "the number of user messages"; here the boundary is the presentation's `operation_ids`, which the agent already declares.

Source: mixar@39b9d27:core/turn_checkpoints.py, mixar@39b9d27:core/checkpoint_timeline.py

must_fix.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_core/src/stack.rs:589-596 says it in its own doc: `same_layer` returns false for every heterogeneous pair, so `plans_overlap` compares only within a layer — 'neither can a door and a crate standing in the doorway'. `Descriptor::clearance` (`descriptor.rs`:46) is documented as 'space that must stay free around the piece' and `descriptor.rs`:678 says it 'is the field that decides anything about space', but nothing in `stack.rs` reads it: grep for `clearance` there returns nothing, and its only non-descriptor readers are validation (`descriptor.rs`:1368) and the composition hash (`composition.rs`:1039). No fixture setter writes `Mount::InOpening { clear }`, so that field has never been exercised either.

items.evidence: Both halves shipped. **Doorway** (d27e452): crates/bevy_emerge_core/src/stack.rs::blocked_openings — the hole is `InOpening`'s `clear` rectangle (not the frame's footprint), vertical is read, another opening and a rider on the door are exempt, `clear: None` reports nothing; checks::Found::doorways carries it as `doorways_in_the_way`. **Clearance** (this pass): stack::blocked_clearances — each `Descriptor::clearance` becomes a rectangle starting at the keeper's own footprint edge, direction = world `yaw + align.front`, extent = the exact projection `half.0*|a0.u| + half.1*|a1.u|` (so a 45-degree piece reserves from its edge, not a circumscribed square), `Around` = four widened bands covering the corners. Tutenel et al. (2010)'s exemption is implemented: an intruder that reserves space itself may share the band, plus `Tiled`/`Decal` intruders, a rider on the keeper, and a piece whose span misses the keeper's. The vertical bound is stated in the doc rather than derived — head height is not in the schema. Carried as `checks.clearances_in_the_way` {"new":[{"keeper","intruder"}],"new_total","total"}. Shared `stack::bodies()` now resolves `resolve_y` once for both checks so they cannot disagree about where a piece is. items.title: Cmd+Z does not take away a map that was just made: there is no map_remove operation
items.evidence: map_create declares Undo::None because `take_back` applies an inverse by calling the SAME operation's commit with it, and the faithful inverse of a create is a removal — which no operation carries. map removal exists only as the chooser's Delete row (chooser.rs confirm_delete_entry, std::fs::remove_file), outside the registry. An agent can therefore make a map and not unmake it. FIXED: map_create's inverse is its own only_as_undo form {remove}, whose inverse is {restore:{name,text}} (file bytes kept in the log); creation lines are project-scoped in undo_target, so they undo by name from any open map; refused while that map is open.
